extracted.intended_audience: general readers and writers interested in Anthony Trollope, autobiographical writing, and Victorian literary practice
extracted.subtask_description: An author's published autobiography that mixes personal memoir with practical statements about how the memoir was prepared and what it should contain — offering explicit rules about truthfulness, scope, editorial handling, and organization of autobiographical material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truthfulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing that I say shall be untrue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author promises to avoid falsehoods in recounting events; statements should be sincere and factually accurate rather than invented or exaggerated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid malice
rubrics_metrics.description: I will set down naught in malice;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recount personal or third-party faults without vindictiveness. Refrain from using the memoir as a vehicle for spiteful attacks; criticism should be measured, not malicious.

rubrics_metrics.name: No undeserved self- or other‑aggrandizement
rubrics_metrics.description: nor will I give to myself, or others, honour which I do not believe to have been fairly won.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attribute honours, praise, or achievements that are not deserved. Present evaluations of oneself and others honestly and modestly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: focus on literary life and its causes
rubrics_metrics.description: It will not be so much my intention to speak of the little details of my private life, as of what I, and perhaps others round me, have done in literature; of my failures and successes such as they have been, and their causes; and of the opening which a literary career offers to men and women for the earning of their bread.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure the autobiography around professional activity (here: literary career), lessons from failures and successes, and practical information useful to others pursuing the same occupation rather than exhaustive private minutiae.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept selectivity and limits of disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: That I, or any man, should tell everything of himself, I hold to be impossible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An autobiographer should recognise and accept that total disclosure is impossible or undesirable; selectivity is legitimate. Omit certain private matters when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect authorial instructions for posthumous publication
rubrics_metrics.description: My father ... said that he had written me a letter, not to be opened until after his death, containing instructions for publication ... 'I would not wish that anything should be added to the memoir.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When editing or publishing a posthumous memoir, follow the explicit wishes of the deceased author about additions, omissions, and timing of publication. If the author permits commentary, confine it to a preface or introductory chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit editorial alteration and be transparent about changes
rubrics_metrics.description: I have suppressed some few passages, but not more than would amount to two printed pages has been omitted. The few footnotes are my father's own additions or corrections. And I have made no alterations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should minimize cuts or changes, record and disclose any suppressed passages or editorial interventions in a preface, and avoid adding material beyond what the author allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize matter into a recognisable and intelligible form
rubrics_metrics.description: I know how to throw my matter into any recognised and intelligible form. I have placed headings to the right-hand pages throughout the book...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear chapterization, headings, and organization so the memoir is readable and coherent. Make structural editorial choices (headings, chapter breaks) explicit to the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasise instructive account of causes and practical lessons
rubrics_metrics.description: …of my failures and successes such as they have been, and their causes; and of the opening which a literary career offers to men and women for the earning of their bread.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame personal anecdotes and recollections to surface causes, lessons learned, and practical advice for readers considering the same career or pursuit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not publish private correspondence without permission
rubrics_metrics.description: My father has not given any of his own letters, nor was it his wish that any should be published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect privacy and the explicit wishes of the subject regarding letters and private documents; omit or secure permission before publishing correspondence.
